author: A Robot
objectives: Students will identify and name the four chambers, valves, and major vessels of the heart.
Students will trace the path of blood through the dual-loop circulatory system.
Students will relate myocardial wall thickness to circulatory pressure demands.

modules.description: Overview of heart anatomy, chambers, and myocardium thickness.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart.
Explain the structural difference in myocardium thickness between ventricles.
instructions: Observe the heart model. Notice the thickness of the left ventricle wall compared to the right.

clips.changeMeaning: Initial display of the heart model.
clips.narration: Welcome. We will explore the anatomy of the human heart, identifying its four chambers and the valves that regulate blood flow.

clips.changeMeaning: Labeling the four chambers of the heart.
clips.narration: Observe the four chambers: right and left atria, and the right and left ventricles. Note the thickness of the left ventricle, designed for systemic pumping.

modules.description: Tracing the dual-loop circulation of blood through the heart.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Trace the path of blood through the dual-loop circulatory system.
Explain the function of heart valves in preventing backflow.
instructions: Follow the blue and red path of blood as it circulates through the heart.

clips.changeMeaning: Visualizing deoxygenated blood entering the heart.
clips.narration: Deoxygenated blood returns from the body via the vena cava, entering the right atrium.

clips.changeMeaning: Visualizing blood flowing to the lungs and returning to the left side.
clips.narration: Blood passes through the tricuspid valve, to the lungs via pulmonary arteries, then returns via pulmonary veins to the left atrium.

clips.changeMeaning: Visualizing oxygenated blood leaving the heart via the aorta.
clips.narration: Finally, the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aortic valve and into the aorta for systemic circulation.
